extracted.intended_audience: donors, partners, policymakers, researchers, and the general public interested in agricultural and food-system research and development
extracted.subtask_description: A high-level organizational/mission page describing CGIAR's research portfolio, thematic priorities, global presence, impact indicators, and resources (dashboards, finance reports, publications). Useful for understanding programmatic priorities and impact metrics for alignment with funding or partnership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research portfolio focus (major global challenges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our research portfolio addresses major global challenges such as climate change, gender and social inequalities, poor-quality diets, rural poverty, environmental degradation, and issues stemming from fragility, conflict, and violence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and proposals should align with these high-level challenge areas; CGIAR frames its work around alleviating these problems through research and development interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Better Diets and Nutrition
rubrics_metrics.description: We co-design and test food system solutions to improve diets and nutrition in low- and middle-income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should demonstrate clear links to diet and nutrition improvements, with context-appropriate co-design and testing in LMIC settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breeding for Tomorrow
rubrics_metrics.description: We develop climate-resilient, nutritious crops and livestock to make food systems more productive, inclusive, and sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on breeding and genetic improvement that deliver climate resilience, nutrition, productivity, and inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: We foster equal, healthy partnerships to share capacity and advance food, land, and water systems with focus on gender, youth, and inclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities should include capacity-strengthening and equitable partnerships, with attention to gender, youth, and inclusion outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climate Action
rubrics_metrics.description: We drive science, innovation, and collaboration to transform food, land, and water systems for a resilient, net-zero, and equitable future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should contribute to resilience, emissions reduction (net-zero aims), and equity in food/land/water systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: We co-create inclusive solutions using AI, data, and tech to boost decisions, policies, and investments for food-land-water transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of AI, data-driven tools, and digital systems is highlighted; solutions should be inclusive and support decision-making, policy and investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food Frontiers and Security
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on three key food systems: fragile/conflict-affected, urban/peri-urban, and island food systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority given to research and interventions tailored to these three frontier contexts, reflecting their unique challenges for food security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Equality and Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: We lead research to advance gender equality, youth opportunities, and inclusion across CGIAR’s Food, Land & Water Systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should include gender and inclusion objectives and measurable outcomes for women and youth empowerment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genebanks (conservation and access)
rubrics_metrics.description: CGIAR genebanks conserve and make available 700k+ crop accessions to support resilient, sustainable and productive farming worldwide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservation, long-term stewardship, and open availability of germplasm are core expectations; genebank-related work should emphasize access and utility for breeding and resilience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multifunctional Landscapes
rubrics_metrics.description: We envision healthy, diverse landscapes that support sustainable food systems, resilient livelihoods, and diets within planetary limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should adopt landscape approaches that balance production, livelihoods, diets and environmental limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: We deliver evidence-based recommendations to strengthen policies, markets and institutions, thereby improving millions of lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should generate actionable, evidence-based policy recommendations and engage with institutions and markets to achieve uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling for Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: We tackle poverty, hunger, and climate risks through science, partnerships, and integrated solutions for greater impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on scalable solutions and partnerships that can increase reach and impact; proposals should describe pathways to scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable Animal and Aquatic Foods
rubrics_metrics.description: We combine livestock and aquatic systems to boost nutrition, cut emissions, and support inclusive, locally tailored solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should integrate livestock/aquatic systems with goals for nutrition, emissions reduction, and local inclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable Farming
rubrics_metrics.description: We boost nutritious food production and protect the environment while tackling climate change, land degradation, pests, and job inequality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions should improve production and nutrition while protecting ecosystems and addressing socio-economic issues like employment and inequality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic reach / global presence
rubrics_metrics.description: CGIAR works across more than 70 countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs are expected to operate at country/regional scale and demonstrate relevance or partnerships in CGIAR geographies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnerships and collaboration scale
rubrics_metrics.description: CGIAR works with more than 3,000 partners around the world to advance the transformation of food, land, and water systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should demonstrate collaborative arrangements and partnerships; multi-stakeholder collaboration is a core operating principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and transparency (dashboards & finance reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: CGIAR is the world’s largest public global agricultural innovation network, producing science for development in an accountable and transparent way. Explore our dashboards; Explore our finance reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expectations include transparent reporting of impact and finances; proposals/units should be prepared to feed into dashboards and public finance reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact metrics reported
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact in numbers: 20 Million farmers reached; 315 Policy changes; 300 Million eating biofortified crops; US$1.34 Trillion generated; 10:1 Return on investment; 3,000+ Plant species conserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CGIAR highlights these headline indicators as measures of success; proposals and reports should track comparable, credible impact metrics and economic returns where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications, dashboards and knowledge products
rubrics_metrics.description: CGIAR produces 1,000+ innovations and 3,400+ knowledge products scaled across Asia, Africa and the Americas; Explore our Publications; Explore our Dashboards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge generation and dissemination (publications, dashboards, knowledge products) are expected outputs; work should include plans for knowledge products and scaling.
